items.item: The grid header names the week with its date range (such as "Week 45 · 2–8 Nov 2026"), every day column shows the weekday and date, and controls move to the previous, next and current week
items.evidence:
Header shows a static '

Week of Nov 9–15, 2026

' and day columns correctly render weekday+date via buildHead() ('MonNov 9'), but there are no previous/next/current-week controls anywhere in the markup or script — DAYS/DATES are hard-coded arrays with no navigation handlers.

items.item: Each shift shows its start and end time in one consistent 24-hour format and the role or station (such as "07:00–15:00 · Cashier"), and a shift that ends after midnight is marked as ending the next day
items.evidence: fmtHour()/fmtTime() produce 12-hour times with 'a'/'p' suffixes (e.g. chip shows '6:45a–2:45p' for Maria Ibarra), not 24-hour format. Chips show only the shift-type label (Open/Mid/Close) and time, not the person's role/station. No logic anywhere checks for or marks an overnight/next-day end (shiftHours() silently adds 24h to negative diffs but nothing renders a 'next day' indicator).

items.item: Each staff row shows the week's scheduled hours against contracted hours (such as "36 / 40 h"), the scheduled figure equals that person's shifts less unpaid breaks, and anyone over or under contract is flagged in words
items.evidence: Row header only shows e.g. '40h scheduled' (buildBody(): Math.round(weeklyHours(person)) + 'h scheduled') — there is no contracted-hours value anywhere in state.staff, no '/ 40h' comparison, and no over/under-contract wording.

items.item: A footer row shows, for each day, the staff count or hours scheduled against the required cover, and days below the requirement are marked in text (such as "Short 1")
items.evidence: buildCoverage() renders only the raw headcount per day plus a generic 'Low coverage' when count < COVERAGE_MIN (e.g. Thursday = 2). The required-cover number (COVERAGE_MIN = 3) is never rendered in the UI, so counts are never shown against the requirement, and the shortfall is not quantified (no 'Short 1' style text).

items.item: The sample data contains at least one rule conflict, such as overlapping shifts for one person or less than 11 hours' rest between a closing and the next opening shift, shown on the affected cell with a written reason
items.evidence: state.staff shifts allow only one shift per person per day (no overlap possible), and manual check of all close→next-shift gaps (e.g. Yuki Sat close 15:00–23:00 → Sun mid 10:00–18:00 = 11h, Omar Fri close 15:00–23:00 → Sat mid 12:00–20:00 = 13h) shows no <11h rest gap. No conflict-detection code or written-reason markup exists anywhere in the script.

items.item: Approved leave, days off and public holidays appear as labelled cells (such as "Annual leave", "Day off") that look different from an empty, unscheduled cell
items.evidence: Approved leave does get a distinct chip (cellContent(): type 'leave' renders '.chip-leave' with label 'Time off' / 'Approved', visible on Omar Haddad/Thu). However type 'off' (day off) is rendered identically to a truly empty cell — cellContent(): 'if (!shift || shift.type === "off") return cell-empty ... "Not scheduled"' — so days off are visually and semantically indistinguishable from unscheduled cells, and there is no public-holiday concept at all.

items.item: The week's status (Draft or Published) is shown, and publishing goes through a confirmation that names the week and the number of unresolved conflicts or warnings
items.evidence: Status badge '#status-badge' correctly toggles 'Draft'/'Published' text via applyLockState(). But the publish-btn click handler flips state.status directly and calls showToast('Published to the team') with no confirmation step at all — no dialog naming the week or reporting conflict/warning counts (none exist to report, per item 5).

items.item: The grid is a <table> with staff names as row headers and days as column headers, and each shift or empty cell is keyboard-reachable with an accessible name that includes the person and the date (such as "Add shift, Lan Pham, Tue 3 Nov")
items.evidence: Markup is a real <table class="roster"> with <th scope="row" class="row-staff"> per staff and <th> day headers — good. Cells are keyboard-reachable (tabindex="0" role="button", Enter/Space handlers). But aria-label is built as `person.name + ', ' + DAYS[dayIndex] + ', ' + (...)`, e.g. 'Maria Ibarra, Mon, Open' — it uses only the weekday abbreviation, never the date number from the DATES array, so the accessible name omits the date.

items.item: A week with no shifts yet shows a message with a way to start (such as "Copy last week"), and a loading state and a load error with a retry button exist
items.evidence: state.staff is hard-coded with shifts already populated; there is no empty-week code path, no 'Copy last week' affordance, and no loading or error/retry UI anywhere in the markup or script — render() runs synchronously against the static in-memory state.

notes: This is a custom-styled roster (navy/kraft/mustard/pine/brick/denim palette, Space Grotesk + IBM Plex Sans) rather than a generic admin template — no greeting header, KPI tiles, gradients, glass, emoji icons, rainbow statuses, sidebar promo, decorative charts, or oversized radii were found, so the 'tells' list is empty. The core interaction model (click/keyboard a cell → popover editor with segmented shift-type buttons and time inputs, toast confirmations, sticky header/first column) is well executed, but the screen is missing most of the roster-specific business logic the checklist probes for: week navigation, 24h time formatting, per-shift role display, overnight-shift marking, contracted-hours comparison, quantified coverage-vs-requirement, rule-conflict detection, day-off vs empty-cell distinction, publish confirmation, date-inclusive accessible names, and empty/loading/error states. Automated audit (score 64/100) separately flags real contrast failures (20 instances ~2:1, e.g. the sr-only 'Not scheduled' text) and a too-wide type/radius scale.
